blocks.text: The page for Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and Endpoint resources (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources) has slightly different names based on the Zscaler products licensed for your organization:

blocks.item: If your organization has licensed only Endpoint DLP, this page is called DLP Resources.
If your organization has licensed only Endpoint Context, this page is called Endpoint Resources.
If your organization has licensed both Endpoint DLP and Endpoint Context, this page is called DLP & Endpoint Resources.

blocks.text: This article explains the differences in functionality between all three versions of the page.
To learn more about accessing Endpoint Context for your organization, contact Zscaler Support.

Creating a resource is the first step in setting up Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and in customizing Endpoint Context data for your organization. For the former, you can create resources for network shares, printers, removable storage devices, and applications; for the latter, you can specify application details.

For Endpoint DLP, you can use the resources you create to configure a policy that protects your organization from data loss by monitoring and taking action on sensitive data that end users interact with on endpoints (i.e., printing, saving to removable storage devices, saving to network shares, or uploading to personal cloud storage accounts). The DLP resources are associated with rules that use Zscaler custom and predefined DLP engines to detect sensitive data, allow or block activities, and notify your organization's auditor when a user's activity on an endpoint triggers an Endpoint DLP rule.
Additionally, you can group resources by category or theme with resource tags, depending on the products that are licensed for your organization.

The Zscaler service automatically supports Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, iCloud for macOS, and OneDrive personal cloud storage accounts. No extra configuration is available for those services as DLP resources.
To learn more, see Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Zscaler Endpoint DLP and About Endpoint Context.
DLP and endpoint resources provide the following benefits and allow you to:

blocks.item: Create rules to monitor and prevent the leakage of sensitive data on endpoints.
Customize endpoint application data for Endpoint Context.
Monitor printing, saving to removable storage devices, saving to network shares, and saving to personal cloud storage accounts.
Use Zscaler custom and predefined DLP engines to detect and take action on sensitive data.

blocks.text: You can use one of the following pages to create DLP and endpoint resources in the Zscaler Admin Console (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources):

blocks.item: About the DLP Resources Page
The DLP Resources page is available if your organization has licensed Endpoint DLP but not Endpoint Context.
On the DLP Resources page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources), you can view and add the following resources:
Network Shares
On the Network Shares page, you can do the following:
Search for a network share.
Import network shares via CSV file.
Add and configure a network share.
Modify the table and its columns.
View a list of all configured DLP network shares for your organization. For network shares, you can see the following:
Name: The network share's name. You can sort this column.
Server Name: The name of the server where the network share is located.
Edit or delete a network share.
Go to the Network Share Tags page.
Go to the Printers page.
Go to the Printer Tags page.
Go to the Removable Storage Devices page.
Go to the Removable Storage Device Tags page.
Go to the Endpoint Applications page.
Go to the Endpoint Application Tags page.
Network Share Tags
On the Network Share Tags page, you can do the following:
Search for a network share tag.
Add and configure a network share tag.
Modify the table and its columns.
View a list of all configured DLP network share tags for your organization. For network share tags, you can see the following:
Tag Name: The network share tag's name. You can sort this column.
Count: The number of network shares associated with the tag.
Description: The network share tag's description.
Edit or delete a network share tag.
Go to the Network Shares page.
Go to the Printers page.

Endpoint Applications
To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
On the Endpoint Applications page, you can do the following:
Search for an application.
Add a Windows application.
Add a macOS application.
Modify the table and its columns.
Select the filtering options for the endpoint applications in the table.
Filter by Operating System or Application Type.
View a list of all configured applications for your organization. For applications, you can see the following:
Name: The name of the application.
Operating System: The OS that the application uses.
Original File Name: (Windows only) The original file name of the executable. This name is located on the Details tab in the Properties for the executable file in Windows.
Bundle ID: (macOS only) The bundle identifier that uniquely identifies the application.
File Name: The name of the executable that runs the application.
Digitally Signed: The setting to indicate whether the application file must be digitally signed by a trusted provider (i.e., Any, Yes, or No).
Application Type: The application type as determined by the Zscaler service:

Well-Known: Applications that are frequently seen within the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) security cloud. This is a dynamic classification that includes more applications as they become more prevalent over time.
Discovered: Applications that are discovered on endpoints by the Zscaler service.
Custom: Applications added to a tenant by an administrator.
Edit or delete an application.

About the Endpoint Resources Page
The Endpoint Resources page is available if your organization has licensed Endpoint Context but not Endpoint DLP.
On the DLP & Endpoint Resources page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint DLP Resources), you can view and add the following resources:
Endpoint Applications
On the Endpoint Applications page, you can do the following:
Search for an application.
Add a Windows application.
Add a macOS application.
Filter by Operating System or Application Type.
View a list of all configured applications for your organization. For applications, you can see the following:
Name: The name of the application.
Operating System: The OS that the application uses.
Original File Name: (Windows only) The original file name of the executable. This name is located on the Details tab in the Properties for the executable file in Windows.
Bundle ID: (macOS only) The bundle identifier that uniquely identifies the application.
File Name: The name of the executable that runs the application.
Digitally Signed: The setting to indicate whether the application file must be digitally signed by a trusted provider (i.e., Any, Yes, or No).
Application Type: The application type as determined by the Zscaler service:

Well-Known: Applications that are frequently seen within the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) security cloud. This is a dynamic classification that includes more applications as they become more prevalent over time.
Discovered: Applications that are discovered on endpoints by the Zscaler service.
Custom: Applications added to a tenant by an administrator.

Endpoint Application Risk Level: The calculated risk level of the application based on multiple properties and behaviors, including static and dynamic properties of the application. Risk is an independent property and can change based on the latest data. The Zscaler service uses four risk levels:
Unknown: All applications might initially appear as an unknown risk until the risk identification and quantification process by the Zscaler service is complete.
High: The application presents a high risk, based on analysis by the Zscaler service.
Medium: The application presents a medium risk, based on analysis by the Zscaler service.
Low: The application presents a low risk, based on analysis by the Zscaler service.
Modify the table and its columns.
Edit or delete an application. You cannot delete applications identified as Discovered or Well-Known by the Zscaler service.
Go to the Endpoint Application Tags page.

Modify the table and its columns.
View a list of all configured application tags for your organization. For application tags, you can see the following:
Tag Name: The name of the endpoint application tag. You can sort this column.
Description: The endpoint application tag's description.
Endpoint Applications: The endpoint applications associated with the tag.
Edit or delete an application tag.
Go to the Endpoint Applications page.
